title: Matching Against Variables
goal: Compare an incoming value against a target variable without shadowing it.

source.attribution: adapted from Day 1 Afternoon: Pattern Matching

hints: An identifier like `expected` inside a match pattern creates a new variable binding, shadowing any variable with the same name outside.
To compare against an existing variable in a match arm, use a match guard with `if`.
explanation: In Rust match patterns, bare names like `expected` create new variable bindings that catch any value. They do not compare against outer variables of the same name. To compare against a local variable, use a match guard `c if c == expected`. Slot 2 requires a literal value like `0`. Using a pattern variable like `target` catches every remaining value.
